text:
kevin: quick heads-up — ran nightly autotune on the new A100 pool and saw a weird smem fragmentation spike for seq_len <= 64 paths. throughput dropped ~18% on batch sizes 4-8 compared to yesterday.

sophia: any profiler traces? sounds like register spills or mismatch in tile selection.

kevin: attaching the microbench output from perf-bot below (shortened) — seemed to switch to a different kernel at runtime that uses tile=128

perf-bot: ````
run: kernel_picker --model=redwood-3b --seq=32 --batch=4 --arch=a100 
selected_kernel: matmul_tile128_sm_shared_preload_v2
occupancy: 37%
regs_per_thread: 68
smem_alloc_bytes: 49152
latency_p50: 12.4ms (baseline 10.5ms)
spills: 1.9%
````

marcus: that kernel's smem footprint is close to the warps*smem_per_warp limit, so fragmentation + register pressure explains the p50 regression. we usually prefer tile=64 for seq<=64. why did the picker choose 128?

anya: probably because the kernel selector weights throughput for larger seqs; the selector heuristic uses a simple threshold at seq=48 for tile switch. autotune might have generalized from mid-length samples.

kevin: here's a diff of the selector rule I tried locally: ````
if seq_len <= 64 and regs_per_thread >= 64:
    prefer_tile = 64
else:
    prefer_tile = 128
````
re-ran & perf-bot result: occupancy jumped to 62% and p50 back to 10.2ms.

sophia: nice. but we should avoid hard thresholds. Can we make a cost model: cost = latency_est(seq, tile) + alpha * spill_penalty(regs_per_thread, tile) + beta * smem_frag(tile, smem_pool) ?

marcus: +1. also need to account for KV cache path — small-seq requests hit the shortpath that prefetches KV into shared memory. If tile is too big, prefetch victimizes other blocks.

kevin: observed exactly that — shortpath prefetch occupancy fell from 0.85 to 0.52 when tile=128 (measured by live kv prefetched pages per SM).

anya: proposed plan:
- adjust kernel_picker to compute an expected_spill_score from regs and liveness (cheap heuristic)
- simulate smem layout for candidate tiles to estimate fragmentation share
- prefer smaller tile when seq percentile < 0.5 and frag_score > threshold
- add metric to dashboard: kernel_switch_count_by_seq_bucket

sophia: also flag models where autotune's sample distribution is skewed. we saw it pick 128 because training samples had a lot of seq=80 traces. need to bias sampling toward production seq hist.

kevin: opened a PR with the heuristic changes and a test harness that replayed 10k requests from prod-q1; local results: overall token/s +6% and shortpath p50 -14%. PR: https://git.redwood-ci/internal/changes/4521

marcus: can we add an integration test that runs on a small A100 in CI to catch regressions? maybe a quick smoke that asserts latency within +-10% of baseline for seq buckets 8/32/128.

anya: yes — I'll add an eng-runtime/ci job that runs the kernel_picker bench against the small matrix of (seq,batch,arch) and fails on >12% regressions.

kevin: awesome. one more note: watch out for register reallocation in newer CUDA runtime — it can change regs_per_thread by +2 and flip the chosen kernel. we'll include a calibration run after driver updates.

perf-bot: autotune job 4521 finished: bench_summary: {"seq_buckets":[8,32,128], "token_s_change":"+6%", "shortpath_p50_change":"-14%"}

sophia: perfect. after the PR lands, let's schedule a canary rollout to 10% of A100 capacity and monitor kernel_switch_count_by_seq_bucket + smem_frag_ratio. :rocket:
